perspective:
Angela Hwang’s available information:

- She and Kevin have been friends since high school and often confide in each other. She noticed Kevin seemed unhappy with his construction job and, feeling concerned, invited him to coffee.
- At coffee, Kevin told her he was “alright, just the usual grind,” then said he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was going through the motions. She asked if he had considered a different job or career path. He said he had thought about it but felt overwhelmed and unsure where to start. She offered to figure it out together; he agreed and thanked her.
- Angela later believed Kevin was considering a career change. Feeling supportive and hopeful, she told him she had found job openings and a career counseling service. He thanked her, said he had been thinking a lot, and mentioned interest in something creative, maybe design or architecture. She encouraged him to check the resources; he said he would.
- Angela then believed Kevin was hesitant. Feeling frustrated and worried, she arranged a meeting with a career coach and told him. He said she didn’t have to do that, appreciated it, but wasn’t sure he was ready. She encouraged him to get a push and a plan. He agreed to give it a shot and thanked her.
- Later, Angela believed Kevin was making progress. Feeling proud and relieved, she asked how things were going with the career coach. Kevin told her the coach was helpful, he had started online design courses, and he felt more confident. She offered more help; he said her being there was enough and he would ask if needed. She said she would always be there.
- Finally, Angela believed Kevin had successfully transitioned. Feeling happy and satisfied, she organized a small celebration party and told him. He thanked her, said he was grateful, and said he couldn’t have done it without her. She replied that he did the hard work and she was glad to support him; they celebrated.

Angela has no access to Kevin’s private thoughts beyond what he directly said or what she observed, nor to events she did not witness or narrator-only information.
